candidate.title: TN-Seq / INSeq
candidate.scope: The assigned middle poster row groups transposon sequencing (TN-Seq; Tn-seq in its primary paper) and insertion sequencing (INSeq). It depicts an MmeI-site-bearing transposon in genomic DNA, MmeI digestion, adapter addition, and a combined PCR and sequencing block ending in insertion-site information. The single drawn route is instantiated as separate method-specific local records to preserve the primary-supported 20-bp Tn-seq versus 16-bp INSeq genomic-tag histories. These record sets are alternative implementations of the grouped row, with no pooling or material transfer between them. The left transposon icon identifies the inserted element and supplies no separate transposition or culture operation. The two MmeI icons describe action at the two ends of one substrate, not circularization or separate sample branches. The adjacent RC-Seq and TC-Seq rows, top-edge labels from another row, and right-edge cytosine structures are outside scope. This schematic-level architecture does not assert identical complete procedures or interchangeability of TN-Seq and INSeq.

states.label: TN-Seq: insertion-site sequences and site-associated counts
features: Visible endpoint: Transposon insertion sites. The primary paper maps bacterial genomic tags to a reference and counts reads for each insertion.

The read identifies a genomic insertion associated with a mutant in the sampled population. Frequency comparisons across populations or time points can support fitness inference; such comparisons are not drawn.
An insertion coordinate alone does not establish loss of gene function; insertion position and mutant representation affect interpretation.

method_scopes.rationale: TN-Seq is the poster spelling of Tn-seq, transposon sequencing, and is distinct from INSeq. The MmeI-based implementation described by van Opijnen, Bodi and Camilli (2009) supports the transposon inverted-repeat sites and 20-bp bacterial tag. Adapter addition is drawn and ligation is clarified by the matching catalogue page. Applicability is resolved for this depicted implementation within the broader Tn-seq family. The INSeq instances implement corresponding schematic purposes with their own material histories, rather than consuming TN-Seq products.
